text.p: An earthquake shook Israel and Lebanon on Wednesday, residents and officials said, but no injuries or damage were immediately reported.
Residents in the Israeli cities Haifa and Tel Aviv said they felt their buildings move.
Yefim Gitterman, a scientist at Israel's Seismological Institute, said the 7.22 a.m. (0422 gmt) quake measured 5.5 on the Richter scale.
In Cyprus, where the tremor was not felt, the geological surveys department said the quake measured 5.6 on the Richter scale.

"We estimate it (the epicentre) was around 350 kilometres (220 miles) east of Cyprus," government geologist Kyriakos Solomi told Reuters, adding that his department was still checking the precise epicentre.
Gitterman said the quake was "short and strong" and aftershocks were felt.
Israel Radio said it was felt in Syria as well.
